findings.issue: An auto-loading project rule file is now factually false because of this spec, and was not fixed.
findings.description: .claude/rules/testing.md opens with 'No test exists anywhere in this repo today (zero files under any *Test* source set, and the convention plugins wire no commonTest/kotlin.test dependency) — there's no existing pattern to extend.' Every clause of that sentence is now wrong: this spec added 9 test files across 4 modules and T-1 wired kotlin-test into both LibraryConventionPlugin and FeatureConventionPlugin. The file then prescribes, as work still to do, exactly what T-1 already shipped ('Wire kotlin.test into commonTest once, in LibraryConventionPlugin/FeatureConventionPlugin') and names three 'currently unverified by anything' first targets. This file is loaded into the context of every future agent in this repo, so the damage compounds. The orchestrator itself logged the governing policy in events.jsonl (category: stale-doc, T-9): 'This staleness was introduced BY this spec and must be fixed before the spec closes' — that policy was applied to .claude/rules/mappers.md and to nothing else.

findings.issue: The Cmd+1/2/3 dispatch path is unreachable by construction, so the human-review item asking a human to verify it cannot be satisfied as written.
findings.description: RectifyWindow.kt:103 declares `val sidePanel: (@Composable ColumnScope.(ShellTab) -> Unit)? = null` as a compile-time constant, and :111 passes `isPanelVisible = sidePanel != null` into handleShellShortcut. handleShellShortcut (:245-254) returns false unconditionally when isPanelVisible is false, so in the shipped binary Cmd+1/2/3 can never select a tab — there is no panel and no code path that makes one. This is CORRECT for AC-31/SC-4, which require exactly that. But it means T-12's open item (3) 'Cmd+1/2/3 dispatch' is not merely unverified in this environment — it is unverifiable in any environment on this build, and a human sent to check it will observe nothing and may wrongly log a defect. SC-3's precondition ('mirroring session is active and the side panel is visible') has no reachable path in this deliverable at all. The pure mapping IS covered: ShortcutToTabTest 3/3 green. The dispatch gate itself has zero coverage (see AF-5).
findings.recommendedTarget: human gate — re-word the T-12 review item, or accept AC-33 on the tested mapping alone and defer live dispatch to android-device-discovery-mirroring

findings.issue: compose-application has no test source set, so every desktop-only decision function is untested and also not manually inspected.
findings.description: T-1 wired kotlin-test into LibraryConventionPlugin and FeatureConventionPlugin only. compose-application applies ApplicationConventionPlugin, which was not touched, so there is no commonTest/desktopTest there — confirmed by the absence of any compose-application entry under build/test-results. Four pieces of real logic therefore have zero automated coverage AND no completed manual inspection: handleShellShortcut (RectifyWindow.kt:245-254 — this is the function that implements SC-4's 'the event is not consumed' clause), ThemeModel.next() (:270-274 — the System->Light->Dark->System cycle that AC-35's toggle actually drives), toThemeMode() (:263-267), and isMacOs() (:238-239). AC-35's persistence half is well covered at the data layer (ThemePreferenceMapperTest 6/6), but its presentation half — the cycle order and the immediate re-render — rests on nothing. The plan anticipated this placement problem for ShellWindowDefaults and solved it by moving the constants into presentation-core-ui; the same move was not made for the dispatch/cycle logic.
findings.evidence: No compose-application directory under any build/test-results path; ApplicationConventionPlugin.kt is absent from git diff development..HEAD --name-only.
findings.recommendedTarget: follow-up — move shortcut-gate and theme-cycle logic into presentation-core-ui (testable) or wire kotlin-test into ApplicationConventionPlugin

findings.issue: The contrast sweep's own anti-omission guard overclaims: two of ThemeColor's 22 tokens are never measured in either palette.
findings.description: PaletteContrastTest has a test literally named 'every pairing in both palettes is measured, none silently skipped' asserting 54 pairings per palette. I counted the builders: 9 text + 4 focus + 4 ink3 + 16 signal + 20 alpha + 1 pop = 54 in each — the arithmetic is honest. But ThemeColor.primaryHover (ThemeColor.kt:51) and ThemeColor.primaryPress (ThemeColor.kt:52) appear nowhere in either builder, in any role. AC-36 names both explicitly in its enumerated token list that must 'meet WCAG AA'. onPrimary-on-primaryHover and onPrimary-on-primaryPress are the pairings a real hovered/pressed primary button paints, and neither has even a frozen baseline. Only onPrimary-on-primary (the resting state) is asserted. The guard test's name makes the omission harder to notice, not easier.
findings.evidence: presentation-core-styling/src/commonMain/kotlin/presentation/core/styling/core/ThemeColor.kt:50-52 declares primary, primaryHover, primaryPress; grep for primaryHover/primaryPress in PaletteContrastTest.kt returns zero matches; PaletteContrastTest.kt assertEquals(54, lightPairings().size).
findings.recommendedTarget: T-2 — add four pairings (onPrimary over primaryHover/primaryPress, both palettes) and raise the count to 56

findings.issue: CORRECTION to the dispatch framing: the line/line2 3:1 hard-fail is in the sealed human-approved plan.json, not only in the orchestrator's brief. The deviation is technically right but overrides a human gate answer and needs explicit ratification.
findings.description: The dispatch brief states the composited line/line2 3:1 requirement 'came from the ORCHESTRATOR'S dispatch brief, not from plan.json — the plan's own wording is looser.' That is not accurate. plan.json .data.survey[0].answer, source 'user-edited', reads: 'Hard-fail on the pairings this shell actually paints (ink/ink2 on bg/chrome/stage/surface at 4.5:1; focus and composited line/line2 at 3:1; onPrimary on primary at 4.5:1)'. The brief faithfully transmitted a sealed human decision. So this is an executor deviation from the human gate, not a brief defect. ADJUDICATION: the deviation is nonetheless the correct engineering call and is handled about as well as it could be. (a) It is arithmetically unsatisfiable — the test itself proves the mechanism in 'compositing an alpha token changes what is measured', and the 16 recorded hairline baselines run 1.19 to 1.58:1 across both palettes. (b) The only remedy is editing tokens AC-36 freezes and scope.out[6] forbids. (c) WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 governs 'visual information required to identify user interface components and states'; a 1dp decorative divider between two panes is not that, so the gate's inclusion of line/line2 in the hard-fail tier was itself the error. (d) The implementation does not hide it: 16 per-line '// WAIVED: <ratio> < 3:1 — AC-40/NFR-11 waived, see DEVIATION above' comments plus a named DEVIATION paragraph in the class KDoc that ends 'Needs a human call.' VERDICT: accept as a satisfaction of AC-30/AC-40/NFR-11, but only by explicit gate ratification — an agent cannot unilaterally overrule a sealed user-edited survey answer.
findings.evidence: plan.json .data.survey[0] (source: user-edited); PaletteContrastTest.kt class KDoc 'DEVIATION from the gate's Tier 1 list' paragraph; the 16 'line over X' / 'line2 over X' frozen() entries with baselines 1.19-1.58.
findings.recommendedTarget: human gate — ratify the downgrade and amend survey Q1-A, or re-open AC-36 for the line tokens

findings.issue: AC-40 is satisfied only under Q1-A's rendered-scope reading; the literal AC fails on four light-mode pairs and the screenshots prove nothing either way.
findings.description: Independently confirmed by looking at all four evidence PNGs: not one signal colour appears anywhere in any of them. DeviceChip(None), CounterBadge(Empty) and StatusIndicator(Offline) all resolve to ink3/seg greys, so the executor's own 'AC-40 evidence is WEAK' admission is understated — the screenshots carry zero AC-40 signal. The real coverage is PaletteContrastTest's signal tier, and it is genuine: dark hard-asserts all 16 signal pairings at 3:1 and they pass with margin (3.51-7.71). Light passes annotate (3.15-3.90) and measure (3.25-4.03) but WAIVES sentFixed (2.70/2.49/2.36/2.92) and warnStillOff (2.19/2.02/1.91/2.36) — eight sub-threshold pairings, not four. So literal AC-40 is NOT met in the light palette. It is met under the Q1-A rendered-scope policy the human gate chose, because this deliverable paints none of them. Recommend recording AC-40 as 'satisfied with waiver' with the eight light pairs handed explicitly to android-device-discovery-mirroring, which is the first spec that will actually paint them.
findings.evidence: Opened execution/T-12/evidence/*.png (all four); PaletteContrastTest.kt lightPairings() frozen() entries for sentFixed and warnStillOff vs darkPairings() nonText() entries for the same tokens.
findings.recommendedTarget: human gate — record AC-40 as satisfied-with-waiver and carry the eight light pairs downstream

findings.issue: The plan's accessibility requirement says the resize handle sets an E-resize cursor; the code sets a Hand cursor.
findings.description: plan.json accessibility A11Y-8 states 'PanelResizeHandle has an 8dp pointer target around a 1dp hairline and sets an E-resize hover cursor.' The 8dp target is real (PanelResizeHandle.kt:31 HandleHitWidth = 8.dp). The cursor is not: PanelResizeHandle.kt:73 sets `.pointerHoverIcon(PointerIcon.Hand)` with an honest inline comment that commonMain has no E-resize icon. Compose Desktop does expose it as PointerIcon(Cursor(Cursor.E_RESIZE_CURSOR)); the smallest fix is a `cursor: PointerIcon = PointerIcon.Hand` parameter the desktop caller overrides. Either fix the code or amend A11Y-8 — today the approved plan and the shipped code state different things, and a hand cursor on a divider reads as 'drag this object' rather than 'resize this edge'.

findings.issue: Two of AC-34's three clauses have no evidence of any kind; the four PNGs cannot supply it.
findings.description: AC-34 has three clauses. (1) 'initial size is 1240x820' — satisfied twice over: ShellWindowDefaultsTest pins DpSize(1240.dp, 820.dp) (5/5 green) and all four evidence PNGs are exactly 1240x820 pixels of rendered content. (2) 'it is user-resizable' and (3) 'cannot be resized below 1024x700' — no evidence. The constant is pinned by test and the AWT application is three lines (RectifyWindow.kt:217-220, window.minimumSize = Dimension(1024, 700)), but nobody has dragged the window. Critically, the evidence PNGs cannot ever close this: they are in-process Compose renders with no OS window chrome at all — no traffic lights, no title bar, no resize grip — which is also why T-12's item (2), the traffic lights sitting inside the 78dp toolbar inset, stays open. Residual risk is low (the AWT path is short and the client properties were confirmed applied by an in-process probe) but non-zero: minimumSize on a non-macOS host measures the outer frame including decorations, so the content floor would be slightly under 700 there. Real human inspection on a 2x Retina macOS display is still required.
findings.evidence: build/test-results/desktopTest/TEST-presentation.core.ui.kit.shell.ShellWindowDefaultsTest.xml tests="5" failures="0"; RectifyWindow.kt:215-221; visual inspection of all four PNGs confirming zero OS chrome.
findings.recommendedTarget: human gate — manual inspection on macOS

findings.issue: Desktop silently loses every existing feature screen. Declared out of scope, but it is a user-visible regression the human should knowingly accept.
findings.description: runDesktopApp() previously composed Window { App() }, which mounted the Navigation3 host and with it splash, onboarding, home, settings and about. It now composes RectifyWindow(), which has no navigation host at all — so on desktop none of those screens is reachable any more. App() is untouched and remains the Android/iOS root. plan.json scope.out[10] names this precisely ('Deciding the fate of the existing template features ... now that the desktop root bypasses NavigationHost — carried forward as an OPEN question, deliberately NOT decided here and deliberately NOT put to this survey'), so it is in-scope-as-declared and not a defect. Flagging because it is the single largest behavioural change in the diff and it was deliberately kept off the survey the human answered.
findings.recommendedTarget: human gate — acknowledge; schedule the open question

findings.issue: The sweep re-derived rather than copied the refiner's figures, and corrected one of them. The plan now carries a superseded number.
findings.description: AS-6 required that the refiner-only chrome/stage figures 'MUST be re-derived by the step-2 sweep, never hardcoded from this document.' That instruction was followed and it caught an error: plan A11Y-4 and survey Q2-A both quote light 'ink2 on chrome ~5.87', while the sweep measures and records 5.75. Every other refiner figure I spot-checked reproduces exactly (light ink3 on bg 3.13 / chrome 2.89 / stage 2.73 / surface 3.39; dark ink 14.74, ink2 6.64, ink3 on bg 3.39 / chrome 3.07; light sentFixed on chrome 2.49). Both 5.87 and 5.75 clear the 4.5:1 text minimum so there is no AC impact — this is the process working. Noting it only so the gate knows plan.json's A11Y-4 table and survey Q2-A hold one stale figure. Separately, A11Y-4 lists dark 'ink on pop 12.19 PASS' but the sweep measures pop only as 'pop under Color.White' — that is survey Q3-A's explicit instruction, not an omission.
findings.evidence: PaletteContrastTest.kt lightPairings() text("ink2 on chrome", baseline = 5.75) vs plan.json .data.accessibility[3] and .data.survey[1].answer.

findings.issue: Two independent copies of the same stub composition, and they have already drifted on a point the human gate decided.
findings.description: RectifyWindowShell.kt's private ShellPreviewToolbar/ShellPreviewStatusBar/ShellPreviewStage and RectifyWindow.kt's RectifyShellContent build the same six toolbar slots and two status-bar slots from the same components with the same literal strings ('No device', 'staged', 'Clear', 'Resolve & Send', the Cmd-Return glyph, 'Waiting for device...', 'Rectify 0.4', 'NO SIGNAL'). ShellToolbar.kt and ShellStatusBar.kt each carry a third near-copy for their own previews. The drift is not hypothetical — it has already happened on a gate decision: survey Q2-A requires 'the shell's own new files use Theme.color.ink2 for any text the shell itself authors', the shipped stage correctly uses ink2 (RectifyWindow.kt:206), and the preview stage uses ink3 (RectifyWindowShell.kt:131). The preview that is supposed to be standing evidence for AC-30/AC-31 therefore paints a token the gate ruled against for shell-authored text. findings.evidence: RectifyWindowShell.kt:93-135 vs RectifyWindow.kt:158-211; RectifyWindowShell.kt:131 color = Theme.color.ink3 vs RectifyWindow.kt:206 color = Theme.color.ink2; plan.json .data.survey[1].answer.

findings.issue: The dot grid issues one draw op per cell; within the stated budget today, worth knowing before the video stream lands on top of it.
findings.description: The Canvas loop calls drawCircle once per grid cell. At the 1240x820 default on a 2x display the stage is roughly 1232x740dp, which is about 77 x 46 = ~3,500 draw ops recorded per draw pass, scaling with window area. The plan's explicit budget ('One Canvas pass over the visible stage area with no per-dot allocation inside the draw loop (precompute the step from LocalDensity)') IS met: cellPx and dotRadiusPx are computed once at :65-67 and Offset is a value class, so the loop allocates nothing. Raising it only because this surface is where a 60fps mirrored device stream will composite downstream; if it ever shows in a profile, a tiled ImageShader brush replaces the whole loop with one drawRect.

Token discipline: zero Color(0x and zero TextStyle( in any new production file; every .dp occurrence is either a private file-level val (HandleHitWidth, StatusBarHeight, ToolbarHeight, PanelHeaderHeight, DotCellSize, DotRadius, and six Preview* constants) or a ShellWindowDefaults public constant, which is the geometry object itself — the DoD's 'no raw .dp at any shell CALL site' holds. Package naming matches the repo's existing convention (bare presentation./data./domain. roots for library modules, dev.rectify.io for compose-application) and test packages mirror their production packages. explicitApi() compliance is proven by construction: the modules compiled and their tests ran.

aggregateDiffReview: Documentation debt is the dominant cross-cutting defect and no single task owns it. The orchestrator wrote the correct policy into events.jsonl for T-9 ('staleness introduced BY this spec must be fixed before the spec closes') and then applied it exactly once, to .claude/rules/mappers.md. Four further doc surfaces this spec invalidated were missed: .claude/rules/testing.md (now false in its opening sentence and still prescribing T-1's completed work), domain-core/README.md:21 (names the deleted MaterialU constant), six module README inventory tables (14 new public declarations unlisted), and .claude/rules/version-catalog-hygiene.md:16 (junit justified by 'no test source set exists yet'). AF-1 / AF-2 / AF-3.

Testability stops at the compose-application boundary. T-1 wired kotlin-test into the library and feature convention plugins only, so handleShellShortcut, ThemeModel.next(), toThemeMode() and isMacOs() are untested — and three of those sit directly under ACs the gate is being asked to sign (AC-33, AC-35, SC-4). The plan solved this exact placement problem once, by putting ShellWindowDefaults in presentation-core-ui so AC-34's constants could be asserted; the same move was not repeated for the desktop decision functions. AF-5.

Duplication: four near-identical copies of the stub toolbar/status-bar composition (RectifyWindowShell.kt previews, RectifyWindow.kt RectifyShellContent, ShellToolbar.kt preview, ShellStatusBar.kt preview) with the same hardcoded strings. They have already drifted on a gate decision — the preview stage paints ink3 while the shipped stage paints ink2, and survey Q2-A requires ink2 for shell-authored text. AF-15.

Security: nothing to flag. The diff adds no network call, no filesystem access beyond java.util.prefs, no permission request, no entitlement, no analytics and no logging of user data. The one new persisted value is an integer panel width. The three apple.awt client-property writes are wrapped in runCatching behind an os.name guard. Koin registrations are appended at the end of each layer group as the plan required. Error handling follows the repo pattern: both new use cases wrap in resultLauncher with Failure.Technical::Preference, and both failure paths in RectifyWindow log and continue so a dead preference store cannot stop the window opening.

Performance: the plan's five budgets all hold. Panel resize is pure Dp arithmetic with only the panel's width modifier invalidated; writes during a drag are provably zero (four distinct ShellStateTest no-change cases); the stage texture precomputes its step and allocates nothing per dot; the width read is in LaunchedEffect(Unit) after first composition so the window paints without waiting on I/O; the test suite ran in ~5 seconds of wall clock. One forward-looking note only: ~3,500 drawCircle ops per draw pass under what will become a 60fps video surface. AF-16.

Dead code: none in the conventional sense — no unused imports, no orphaned functions, no commented-out blocks, no TODO/FIXME/HACK markers anywhere in 45 files. The closest thing is the dispatch path in handleShellShortcut, which is live code that cannot currently execute; that is deliberate forward wiring for the downstream spec, not dead code, but it should be understood as untested forward wiring rather than working behaviour. AF-4.

Pattern consistency: good. Package layout follows the core/ vs source/ rule with no empty core/ directories created; test packages mirror production packages; the new preference follows the full api -> impl -> mapper -> repository -> use case chain in the documented order; KDoc is present and genuinely informative on every public declaration (several comments explain a non-obvious decision rather than restating the signature — the rememberUpdatedState note in PanelResizeHandle and the private-backing-field note in ShellState are both real).

Scope discipline: clean. No adb/idb/device discovery, no annotation/measure/payload/history implementation, no MCP, no iOS work, no new dependencies beyond the three test-only catalog entries. DEMO_MODE remains false. The two logged dispatch deviations (T-1/T-2 not deferred to a terminal wave; T-4..T-7 batched into one worktree) are both reasoned and both produced correct results — T-1 genuinely had to run first, and the T-4..T-7 batch produced a coherent organism with no visible seams between the atom, the regions and the assembling shell. AF-18.

One behavioural change deserves a conscious human decision even though it is formally in scope: desktop no longer reaches splash, onboarding, home, settings or about, because runDesktopApp() swapped Window { App() } for RectifyWindow(). plan scope.out[10] names this and deliberately kept it off the survey the human answered. AF-12.

verdict.summary: The engineering is sound. All 13 tasks are genuinely done against real files, all 49 tests are genuinely green in XML I read myself, scope discipline is clean, token discipline is clean, and the one deliberate technical deviation (T-2's hairline contrast downgrade) is correct and honestly documented. The real defects are documentation debt the spec created and did not clean up, plus two ACs whose live-inspection half was never performed because the environment denied screen access.
verdict.recommendation: Do not close yet. AF-1 and AF-2 are cheap, provable doc fixes that should land before the spec closes under the orchestrator's own stale-doc policy. AF-4, AF-11 and AF-12 need a human decision, not more code. AF-6 and AF-10 are small, well-scoped follow-ups.
